clue.text: Two bits won't start to get you a musical instrument

indicators.note: Two asks for the trimmed bit to be written down a second time in a row
won't start means the word for a bit loses its opening letter

parts.note: an atom is a tiny bit of anything

explanation.surface: A grumble that two coins with no beginning will not buy you a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't start' cuts the A from ATOM, a bit, leaving TOM, and 'Two' doubles it. 'Two bits' looks like an American quarter-dollar, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a hand-beaten drum, so it is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Anything northern upset a certain small group

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the dialect word reads upwards

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything
some can mean a certain, as in some person

explanation.surface: A northerner overturns a particular small group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OWT into TWO. OWT is Yorkshire and Lancashire dialect for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair, the smallest possible group of people.

clue.text: Look, chaps — round, juicy fruit!

indicators.note: round means the men go around the word for look

parts.note: chaps are men
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An exclamation pointing out a plump, juicy fruit to some fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of the fruit's description but is the container signal; LO is an archaic word meaning look.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large, juicy fruit such as a cantaloupe.

clue.text: "Coral Island" is good; "Home and Away" ultimately isn't

parts.note: OK means good, satisfactory
being in means being at home

indicators.note: ultimately isn't means the last letter of the word away is absent

explanation.surface: A TV critic praises one show but not the Australian soap Home and Away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately isn't' drops the final Y of AWAY. Home and Away is a long-running Australian soap shown in Britain; Coral Island is also a children's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is a Japanese island ringed by coral reefs.

clue.text: Fly to Suez regularly? Do!

indicators.note: Do is short for ditto, an order to repeat what has just been written
regularly means taking every other letter of the words to Suez

explanation.surface: A traveller is urged to fly out to the Suez Canal on a regular schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of 'to Suez', T, S, E; 'Do!' (ditto) repeats them.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Leaves wasp in a cheese sandwich

indicators.note: sandwich means the words wasp in a cheese hold the letters between them

explanation.surface: A wasp has crawled into a cheese sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwich' points to waSP IN A CHeese; 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a vegetable eaten for its green leaves.

clue.text: Sadly Australian team's leader is missing extraordinary spinner

indicators.note: sadly means badly, so the letters are mixed up
is missing means the letters of the word is are absent from the mix
leader means the first letter of the team

explanation.surface: Sadly the Australian team's captain is absent, along with its exceptional spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTRALIAN plus T, without I and S, rearranges into the answer. 'spinner' looks like a cricket bowler, but it spins webs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a huge hairy spider, an extraordinary web-spinner.

clue.text: Drug to reverse progress of Ebola virus essentially saved part of body

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: to reverse progress means to send something backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
saved means kept inside, so the disease's name holds the central letter
essentially means the central letter of the word virus

explanation.surface: A drug that halts the spread of the Ebola virus saved a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saved' puts R (middle of virus) into EBOLA, giving EBOLRA, and 'to reverse progress of' turns it into ARLOBE after E.
explanation.definitionFit: The earlobe is the soft lower part of the outer ear.

clue.text: Third of blue-collar labour force disheartened and lacking opportunity

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of blue

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to nab or arrest them

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle is taken out, leaving only the ends of labour force

explanation.surface: A third of the blue-collar workforce feels dispirited and without prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the third letter of blue; 'disheartened' leaves L and E, the ends of 'labour force'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable means not able, lacking the means or chance to do something.

clue.text: Blair debonairly relaxed in academic institution

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters of the two words are let fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Tony Blair strolls smoothly and debonairly around a university building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed' rearranges the fifteen letters of BLAIR and DEBONAIRLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bodleian is the main research library of Oxford University, an academic institution.

clue.text: Petty Officer First Class (Retd) seeing scene of recent war

parts.note: a bosun (bos'n), the boatswain, is a ship's petty officer

indicators.note: Retd, retired, read as retreated, so the letters for first class go backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, written AI

explanation.surface: A retired naval petty officer, first class, has seen action in a recent war.
explanation.walkthrough: '(Retd)' is the reversal signal on first class; BOS'N is the usual shortened spelling of boatswain, a petty officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosnia was a battleground in the Yugoslav wars of the 1990s, recent when the puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Clever fellow's concealed supporter?

parts.note: a bra supports the bust, a crossword staple
something concealed may be tucked away in a box

explanation.surface: Asks whether a clever man is really just a hidden backer.
explanation.walkthrough: A bra hidden in a box is a 'concealed supporter'; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainbox is British slang for a very clever person, a whizz or egghead.

clue.text: Go through Lampeter, heading away, going off east

indicators.note: going off means going bad or exploding, so the remaining letters are rearranged
heading away means the first letter of the town's name is dropped

explanation.surface: Directions for travelling through Lampeter, a Welsh town, then heading off east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading away' drops L, leaving AMPETER, which 'going off' rearranges to PERMEAT before E. Lampeter is a small university town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread or seep through something.

clue.text: State nominates liberal

indicators.note: liberal means free or loose, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A US state puts forward a liberal candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' rearranges NOMINATES; it looks like a political label.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the United States.

clue.text: Shaun stripped, then went ahead and pulled

indicators.note: stripped means the name loses its outer layers, its first and last letters

parts.note: led means went in front, went ahead of others

explanation.surface: Shaun took his clothes off, went first, and dragged something along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' removes S and N from Shaun, leaving HAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauled means dragged or tugged with effort, a synonym of pulled.

clue.text: American teen hacked into newsgroups

indicators.note: hacked means chopped up, so the letters of the word teen are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American teenager breaks into online discussion forums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked' turns TEEN into ENET.
explanation.definitionFit: Usenet is the early internet's network of discussion newsgroups.

clue.text: Soviet revolutionary family has sex in a revolutionary way

indicators.note: in a revolutionary way means turned around, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: kin means family
tups means mates, used of a ram, crudely of people

explanation.surface: A Soviet radical's family makes love in a way that overturns convention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a revolutionary way' reverses KIN TUPS. The definition is witty: a satellite revolves in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik was the Soviet satellite that orbited, or revolved around, the Earth in 1957.

clue.text: You once held mythical creature's foot

indicators.note: held means the archaic pronoun holds the legendary bird inside

parts.note: thee is an archaic form of you
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: You once grasped the foot of a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' is the container signal. 'foot' looks like a body part, a sensible match for a creature, but it is the unit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A trochee is a metrical foot of one stressed syllable then one unstressed.

clue.text: Smelling a rat, old spymaster suppressed then rejected CIA brief

indicators.note: suppressed means held down inside, so the rat holds the old spymaster

parts.note: taken as written
M is the spymaster who runs James Bond

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the cut-short agency's letters run backwards
brief means cut short, losing the final letter of the agency's name

explanation.surface: An old spy chief suspects a traitor and spurns a short report from American intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressed' is the container signal for old spymaster in the rat; 'brief' trims the agency and 'rejected' turns the remainder around. 'Smelling a rat' looks like an idiom but 'Smelling' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means having a strong smell, so smelling in the sense of giving off a scent.

clue.text: Provide backing for top guitar player

indicators.note: top means the first letter is cut off, as in topping a tree

parts.note: a bassist plays bass guitar

explanation.surface: Back up the best guitarist in the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like an adjective meaning best but is a verb removing the first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help or support, to provide backing.

clue.text: Former love, born female, male on the inside

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: on the inside means the man's name sits within the word for born

parts.note: nee, the feminine form of French born, marks a woman's maiden name
Tim is a man's name, standing for a male

explanation.surface: A past lover, born a woman, was a man inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the inside' is the container signal. NEE is used before a married woman's maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, as in a one-time champion.

clue.text: Student swallowed poison to put an end to it

definitions.text: to put an end to it

indicators.note: swallowed means the word for poison takes the student inside

parts.note: to infect is to poison or contaminate
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student drank poison in order to end it all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'with student swallowed, poison'. The suicide reading misleads: to inflect a word is to add an ending to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflect a word is to change its form, often by adding an ending, as in plurals.

clue.text: In short, it's no country for the many

parts.note: the abbreviation No. is short for numero, Latin-derived for number
US, the United States, is a country

explanation.surface: Echoes the film title No Country for Old Men, with the many in place of the old.
explanation.walkthrough: No. for number is an abbreviation of numero, so 'in short' it is NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous means existing in large numbers, as the many are.

clue.text: 4 thus gives us our instruction to leave

definitions.meaning: four with its F taken away leaves our, so the phrase is the order that does this
a rude command telling someone to go away

explanation.walkthrough: The 4 is the number four, not 4-across: remove its F and our remains. EFF is the name of the letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: Eff off is a euphemistic version of a vulgar order to go away.

clue.text: Hostility to English eccentric

parts.note: flak means hostile criticism

explanation.surface: An odd character is hostile towards the English.
explanation.definitionFit: A flake is informal slang for an eccentric or unreliable person.

clue.text: I sit and chop nuts, hungry, marginalised and unworldly

indicators.note: marginalised means pushed to the edges, so the hungry word forms the margins around the mixture

parts.note: unsated means not yet satisfied, still hungry

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of I sit and chop are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sits and chops nuts while hungry and left out of things, naive about the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' is the anagram signal and 'marginalised' the container one: the hungry word forms the margins. 'nuts' looks like food to chop, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated means naive and lacking worldly experience.

clue.text: Villains vandalise van, kindly keeping back contents

indicators.note: keeping back means the inner run is read backwards
contents means what lies inside the words vandalise van kindly

explanation.surface: A request that vandals spare a van and politely leave what it is carrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' takes SEVANK from vandaliSE VAN Kindly and 'keeping back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Knaves are dishonest rogues, villains in old-fashioned speech.

clue.text: High-class carbon steel alloy

indicators.note: an alloy is a blend of metals, so carbon and the letters of steel are mixed together

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A description of a superior grade of carbon steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alloy' mixes C with STEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Select means choice or exclusive, of high quality.
